name: How much one record in a workshop agent's memory matters
summary: Places one journal row or memory entry of a workshop agent on four concrete levels, from routine work that went as expected to an owner's standing instruction or an emergency stop. Code maps the probability-weighted level onto the 1-to-10 importance its memory retrieval combines with recency and relevance.

importance.instructions: How much does the record in `record` matter to what the agent named in `agent` should remember about its work for the owner? `record.source` says whether it is a journal row or a memory entry, `record.kind` names what kind of row or entry it is, `record.text` is what it says, and `record.status` is a finished command's exit status when there is one. Judge the record alone, by what happened, not by how long or how technical the text is.

criteria.summary: Routine work that went as expected.
signals: a request or report about ordinary work that finished normally
a check or a scheduled job that passed
a question the agent answered from what it read

criteria.summary: A failure, or a correction from the owner.
signals: a command or test that failed, timed out, or did not finish
the owner turned down a command the agent proposed, or the host refused one
the owner corrected how the agent did something

criteria.summary: A change that was merged or rejected.
signals: the owner merged one of the agent's changes
the owner rejected a change at the Merge station
a change now waits for the owner's review

criteria.summary: An owner's standing instruction, or an emergency stop.
signals: the owner told the agent to always or never do something from now on
the owner asked the agent to remember a fact
the owner stopped, paused, or retired the agent
